chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, a non-Arab man from my community recites the Quran in a non-Arab manner, so the angels raise it up as Arabic.'
ai.seo_question: Does a non-Arab Muslim's Quran recitation need to be in perfect Arabic to be accepted by angels?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the universality of the Quran by affirming that non-Arab Muslims (Ajam) are not required to master classical Arabic pronunciation to achieve spiritual validity. The angels' act of 'elevating' the recitation signifies divine acceptance of the effort and intent, bridging the gap between linguistic diversity and liturgical purity, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of prayer for non-Arabs.
